headline: Facebook desktop version restored after 2-hour global outage
summary: Users in Bangladesh and worldwide faced login issues and feed updates failures before services returned to normal around 3:30 PM on Sunday.
details: Facebook's desktop version experienced a significant outage on Sunday, July 19, starting around 1:40 PM. The disruption lasted approximately two hours before returning to normal around 3:30 PM.
Users in Bangladesh and other countries worldwide reported being unable to log in, slow website loading times, and feeds that would not update.

According to DownDetector, reports of issues surged shortly after the start of the outage. The Manchester Evening News reported a significant spike in searches for 'Facebook down' around 9 AM local time in the UK.
Affected users saw a message stating, 'Account temporarily disabled. Your account is currently unavailable due to site problems. We hope to resolve the issue soon. Please try again in a few minutes.'
DownDetector data indicated that 50% of users experienced website access issues, 20% reported login problems, and another 20% reported issues with the news feed and timeline.
The outage also reportedly affected some users on Instagram, another Meta-owned platform, although Meta has not yet released an official statement regarding the cause of the cause of the outage.
The service has since been restored for the majority of users globally.

headline: 4 children die in 24 hours as measles outbreak worsens in Bangladesh
summary: A total of 788 children have died since March 15, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
details: Four children died within the last 24 hours due to measles symptoms, according to a regular report by the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) released Sunday.
Three of the deceased children were from the Dhaka division, while one was from the Sylhet division.
Since March 15, a total of 788 children have died, including 693 who died with measles symptoms and 95 from confirmed cases of measles.
In the last 24 hours, 938 more people showed symptoms of measles across the country.
The total number of people with measles symptoms since March 15 has reached 117,648, with 14,431 confirmed cases.
Over 101,000 patients with measles symptoms have been admitted to hospitals since March 15, of which 96,521 have been discharged.
caption:
788 children dead since March 15. The measles outbreak in Bangladesh is claiming lives at an alarming rate.

Four children died within the last 24 hours due to measles symptoms, according to a regular report by the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) released Sunday.

Three of the deceased children were from the Dhaka division, while one was from the Sylhet division.

Since March 15, a total of 788 children have died, including 693 who died with measles symptoms and 95 from confirmed cases of measles.

In the last 24 hours, 938 more people showed symptoms of measles across the country.

The total number of people with measles symptoms since March 15 has reached 117,648, with 14,431 confirmed cases.

Over 101,000 patients with measles symptoms have been admitted to hospitals since March 15, of which 96,521 have been discharged.
